#### Why $n-1$ and not $n$?
The sample mean $\bar{x}$ is computed from the same data, so the
deviations $(x_i-\bar{x})$ are not fully independent — they sum to
zero. Using $n-1$ (Bessel's correction) makes $s^2$ an unbiased
estimator of the true population variance. In this descriptive
statistics course, we use the **sample** formulas (`.S`) by default
because real business data are almost always samples. The population
variants (`.P`) are shown for completeness.
